section_summary.extract_value: This results section reports that, at the between-persons level, greater mean exposure to non-body focused others over the week predicted higher body appreciation, while exposure to body-focused others showed a negative trend (p = .07). At the within-person level, daily increases in exposure to non-body focused others predicted higher body appreciation, whereas daily deviations in exposure to body focused others did not; lagged analyses showed limited predictive effects. The section does not label any study number or provide sample, demographic, measurement, or BMI-related details.
section_summary.evidence_source: "At the between-persons level, mean exposure to non-body focused others (Hypothesis 1a) positively predicted body appreciation over the week, and mean exposure to body focused others (Hypothesis 1b) negatively predicted body appreciation at a trendlevel, p = .07 (Table 2)." "Within-persons, daily deviations in exposure to non-body focused others (Hypothesis 2a) positively predicted body appreciation, but daily deviations in exposure to body focused others (Hypothesis 2b) was not a predictor, p = .68."
